newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares down despite Ciller's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares down despite Ciller's remarks.

text.p: Istanbul shares were lower in afternoon trade on Monday despite remarks by deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller that the Islamist-led coalition would survive.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 was down by 1.5 percent at 1,444 at 1155 GMT.
"We will continue to work with stability," Ciller told reporters after meeting Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Daily Hurriyet quoted former industry and trade minister Yalim Erez, who resigned on Saturday, as saying that the government would collapse in a week time with the help of other dissidents from the junior coalition partner, the True Path Party (DYP) of Ciller.

"The political tension has not yet been eliminated. The index may fall to 1,430 levels, but it may rise to over 1,440 level again on reaction buys and get stuck in a narrow band between 1,440-1,450," said Serdar Surer from Ekinciler securities.
Okan Alpay from Interyatirim said the index was expected to face support at 1,430 and 1,420 levels.
